adoram-2.title: Adoram
adoram-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adoram-2.note: One of 3 men called Adoram. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Chronicles.

ahiah.title: Ahiah
ahiah.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
ahiah.note: Ahijah, the prophet from Shiloh. He tore his own cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam, for the ten tribes about to be torn from Solomon's line, and after Solomon died the kingdom split just that way.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

arabia.title: Arabia
arabia.note: Paul says he went away into Arabia for a time after his conversion, and in the New Testament the word covers the region south and east of Judea.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

asaph.title: Asaph
asaph.about: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaph.note: A Levite David put in charge of one of the temple choirs. Twelve psalms carry his name, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, which means either he wrote them or a guild of musicians kept his name for generations.

baalath.title: Baalath
baalath.note: Dan was given this town, and Solomon later fortified it as one of his store cities. The name means mistress or lady.

beth-horon.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon.note: Twin towns on the pass from the coastal plain up into the hill country. Joshua's army came this way chasing the Canaanite coalition in the battle where the sun stood still.

bezaleel.title: Bezaleel
bezaleel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
bezaleel.note: God named him and filled him with his Spirit to design and build the tabernacle and everything in it, the ark of the covenant included. He is the first person in the Bible described as filled with the Spirit.

boaz-2.title: Boaz
boaz-2.note: Named twice, in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elath.title: Elath
elath.note: A port on the Gulf of Aqaba near Ezion-geber. Solomon held it, Edom took it back, Uzziah recovered it for Judah, and Syria finally got it. Modern Eilat keeps the name.

ezion-geber.title: Ezion-geber
ezion-geber.note: Solomon built his fleet here, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Elath, to sail for Ophir, and Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked here later. Nelson Glueck dug Tell el-Kheleifeh in the 1930s and called it the site, though later work on the pottery has kept the question open.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hamath-zobah.title: Hamath-Zobah
hamath-zobah.note: Solomon captured it and rebuilt it as a store city, and whether it is Hamath on the Orontes or a separate stronghold tied to Zobah is disputed.

heman.title: Heman
heman.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
heman.note: David put him among the chief musicians over the worship, a Levite. Psalm 88, one of the darkest laments in the book, is credited to him.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

horeb.title: Horeb
horeb.note: Another name for Sinai, where Moses met God at the burning bush and Israel received the law, and where Elijah later ran and heard God in a still, small voice after the wind, earthquake and fire.

hur.title: Hur
hur.about: Aaron's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hur.note: He helped Aaron hold up Moses's arms while Israel fought Amalek, since Israel won as long as those hands stayed up. When Moses went up Sinai for the law, Hur was left in charge with Aaron.

huram.title: Huram
huram.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
huram.note: Chronicles spells the king of Tyre this way. He is the Hiram who sent materials for Solomon's temple.

huram-2.title: Huram
huram-2.about: Syrian living at the time of United Monarchy
huram-2.note: The bronzeworker the king of Tyre sent to make the temple's furnishings, spelled Huram in Chronicles and Hiram elsewhere.

iddo-2.title: Iddo
iddo-2.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
iddo-2.note: A seer whose writings Chronicles cites for the reigns of Solomon, Rehoboam and Abijah. The writings themselves are lost.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jachin-3.title: Jachin
jachin-3.note: Named twice, in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

japha.title: Japha
japha.note: The Hebrew name for Joppa, the port that is Jaffa today. Solomon's cedar came in by sea there, and so did Ezra's timber for the second temple, and Jonah sailed from it toward Tarshish. The Amarna letters already mention its guarded gate.

jeduthun.title: Jeduthun
jeduthun.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
jeduthun.note: David put three chief musicians over temple worship, Heman, Asaph and Jeduthun. Several psalms carry Jeduthun's name in their headings.

jeroboam.title: Jeroboam
jeroboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
jeroboam.note: Solomon's official who led the ten northern tribes out after Rehoboam refused to lighten the labour his father had laid on them. To stop his people going back to Jerusalem to worship, he set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan with a priesthood of his own. Every northern king after him gets measured against that sin.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

moriah.title: Moriah
moriah.note: Abraham was told to take Isaac to the land of Moriah and offer him there. Chronicles puts Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. Jewish tradition has long taken the two as the same ridge.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nathan.title: Nathan
nathan.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan.note: The prophet who told David the story of the rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, let David condemn the man, and then turned it on him over Bathsheba and Uriah. Earlier he had brought God's promise that David's house would last forever. When David was dying, Nathan helped put Solomon on the throne ahead of a rival half-brother.

nebat.title: Nebat
nebat.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nebat.note: Jeroboam's father, and he is only ever named in "Jeroboam son of Nebat," the phrase the books of Kings use again and again for the king blamed for making idol worship the habit of the north.

ophir.title: Ophir
ophir.note: It was the gold that made Ophir famous across the ancient world. Solomon's ships, sailing with Hiram of Tyre, brought it back in quantity, and the place itself was likely in southern Arabia or along the Red Sea.

ornan.title: Ornan
ornan.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ornan.note: The Jebusite who owned the threshing floor David bought to build an altar and stop the plague, the ground where Solomon's temple later stood. Ornan offered it for nothing, and David insisted on paying. He is also called Araunah.

parvaim.title: Parvaim
parvaim.note: Solomon got gold from Parvaim to overlay the temple, and nobody is sure where that was. Guesses run from Arabia to India. Some think the word just means the east.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

pharaoh-3.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-3.note: Solomon married his daughter. Pharaoh is a title rather than a name, and the record never gives this one any other.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

rehoboam.title: Rehoboam
rehoboam.about: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy
rehoboam.note: Solomon's son, and he lost most of the kingdom in his first days on the throne. The northern tribes asked him to lighten the heavy labour his father had laid on them. He turned down the older advisers and threatened them with worse.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

shilonite.title: Shilonite
shilonite.note: A man from Shiloh. It is what they called the prophet Ahijah, who tore his cloak into twelve pieces to show that God would split Solomon's kingdom.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

tadmor.title: Tadmor
tadmor.note: It was Solomon's city out in the desert northeast of Damascus, on the caravan routes, and the Greeks and Romans knew it as Palmyra.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uri.title: Uri
uri.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
uri.note: Bezalel's father. Bezalel was the craftsman God picked to build the tabernacle and its furnishings.

zereda.title: Zereda
zereda.note: Named once, in 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.
